title: EXCLUSIVE: Moonshot execs in talks to settle dispute with shareholder ahead of planned IPO, people say
source_used: Startup Fortune and BigGo Finance, both relaying a Reuters exclusive; Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401)
key_facts: Reuters reported on 11 Oct 2026 that top executives at Moonshot AI, the Alibaba-backed maker of the Kimi chatbot, are in talks to settle a legal dispute with a shareholder demanding compensation.

The shareholder is Recurrent.ai, an earlier startup co-founded in 2016 by Moonshot chief executive Yang Zhilin and chief technology officer Zhang Yutao; Recurrent and some of its investors accuse them of misrepresentation and of enriching themselves at Recurrent's expense.
The case is in arbitration in Hong Kong; it dates to 2024 and centres on whether required waivers were obtained before Moonshot was founded.
Reuters reported the former investors are seeking additional equity compensation that could amount to more than $700 million based on a prior $30 billion valuation of Moonshot.
A March letter from Recurrent's lawyers, seen by Reuters, makes the allegations without evidence; Reuters could not verify it.

Moonshot confidentially filed for a Hong Kong listing in September, targeting the first quarter of 2027; sources say the dispute is not expected to derail the IPO but could complicate it, and it is unclear whether a settlement is imminent.
In 2024 Moonshot's lawyer said the case 'lacks both legal and factual basis'; Moonshot declined to comment to Reuters.
Our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried Bloomberg's report that Moonshot closed a final private round at about $50 billion and is heading for a Hong Kong listing.
quote_evidence: Reuters reported on October 11 that top executives at Moonshot AI, the Alibaba-backed maker of the Kimi chatbot, are in talks to settle a legal dispute with a shareholder demanding compensation, just as the company pushes toward a Hong Kong listing.
The letter does not provide evidence for these allegations. Reuters was unable to independently verify the accuracy of the letter's contents.
Sources say the dispute is not expected to derail the IPO, but could complicate the listing process.
why_it_matters_hint: An unresolved shareholder claim of more than $700 million could raise governance questions for investors in Moonshot's planned Hong Kong listing.
event_date: Reuters exclusive of 11 Oct 2026; dispute dates from 2024
notes: Reuters original blocked (HTTP 401); text read on Startup Fortune and BigGo Finance, which both relay the Reuters exclusive. Allegations are unproven and denied in 2024 by Moonshot's lawyer.
